baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction fima anta min dhikraha places the addressee in relation to an act of making the feminine referent present again.
baseline_models.mechanism: The inward-recall and reminder branches make dhikraha a re-presencing operation; the question probes what place or agency anta has within that operation.

activation_trace.role: Recall after absence supplies inward re-presencing and makes dhikra a cognitive event.
A reminder causes renewed presence and makes the addressee's relation potentially causative.

changed_reading.before: A vague question about remembering an unspecified feminine referent.
changed_reading.after: A question about the addressee's standing in the process that brings the referent back into awareness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Dhikraha can be the referent's passage onto the tongue, while fima anta min asks how the addressee belongs to that mentioning.
baseline_models.mechanism: The voiced-mention branch shifts the focus from private memory to a speech-role without yet specifying whether that role is disclosure, naming, or admonition.

activation_trace.role: Mention running on the tongue supplies the public speech-act whose relation to anta is questioned.

changed_reading.after: It can be voiced mention, so the question also probes the addressee's function in speaking of it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The received report of Moses becomes an example that transfers one case into admonition for a fear-responsive hearer; the closing sequence repeats that receptive condition and names the addressee a warner. Voiced dhikra is therefore warning-shaped communication rather than bare information.

activation_trace.role: Voiced mention anchors the activated warning-speech model in the focus.
A renewed report supplies discourse material that can be transmitted to the addressee.
Taking one condition as an example for another converts report into an admonitory mechanism.
Fear with awe marks the audience in whom the narrated example operates.
Warning that awakens caution assigns the addressee an operative speech-role.
The repeated fear-with-awe condition closes the report-to-warning audience loop.

structural_cues: The Moses report at 79:15 ends as an example for one who fears at 79:26; the same recipient condition returns in 79:45.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies report to example and warner to fear-responsive hearer; I infer that these frame dhikra as the same admonitory speech-act. A live alternative is generic mention without narrative form.

changed_reading.before: The addressee may merely mention the referent.
changed_reading.after: His relation is to turn mention into warning capable of moving a fear-responsive hearer, not to satisfy curiosity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Arrival is followed by the human being's same-root recollection of personal striving and by unveiled consequence. The focus reminder thus acts prospectively: it prepares a future involuntary self-recollection rather than supplying a date.

activation_trace.role: The reminder branch anchors a present act intended to restore future awareness.
Arrival and occurrence supply the temporal trigger that precedes recollection.
Recall after absence supplies the future cognitive event anticipated by dhikraha.
Work and acquisition give that recollection its personal behavioral content.
Disclosure and exposure couple remembered action with unveiled consequence.

structural_cues: The ordered sequence at 79:34-36 moves from arrival to recollection of striving to visible consequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies arrival, remembering one's striving, and exposure in sequence; I infer that 79:43's reminder prepares that self-recollection. Alternatively, the repeated root may provide lexical cohesion without a preparatory arrow.

changed_reading.before: Dhikraha concerns recalling or reporting when the event occurs.
changed_reading.after: Dhikraha is a present reminder aimed at the later moment when each person remembers their own striving under exposure.

context_deltas.mechanism: A request seeks the event's fixed mooring; the next lines assign its endpoint to the Lord and assign the addressee warning for the awe-responsive hearer. The focus question separates fixing the terminus from making the event present as warning.

activation_trace.role: Voiced mention supplies the communicative operation whose proper agent-role is being delimited.
Reminder supplies the positive function left to the addressee after endpoint-fixing is excluded.
Questioning as request supplies the demand to which the focus responds.
Fixity and settledness make the requested object a determinate anchoring point.
Lordship and ownership assign authority over the endpoint away from the addressee.
The limit at which a thing ends supplies the withheld terminus.
Warning that awakens caution positively defines the addressee's function.
Fear with awe identifies the audience for whom that reminder-function becomes effective.

structural_cues: 79:42 asks for its mooring; 79:43 interrupts; 79:44 redirects its endpoint; 79:45 restricts anta to warning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies demand and fixity, Lord and endpoint, then addressee and warning; I infer that the contrast distributes epistemic and functional roles. A live alternative is a local rebuke of pointless questioning rather than a general jurisdictional boundary.

changed_reading.before: The question may ask generally why the addressee speaks of the event.
changed_reading.after: It delimits roles: fixing the endpoint is outside his relation, while making it present as warning is his relation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the secondary r-s-w branch about firming a report and mentioning an edge beneath the surface mooring image. It remains valid because 79:32 and 79:42 repeat r-s-w and the focus anchors the move in voiced dhikr; render it only as a lexical-material echo, not as the direct sense of mursaha.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The outlier returns to the focus's voiced-mention branch: dhikraha is an attempt to give the referent a verbal handle.

activation_trace.role: Mention on the tongue anchors the possible discursive handling of the event.
Literal fixing and settling of mountains supplies the material image of anchoring.
Firming a report and mentioning its edge turns the requested mooring into a possible demand for a stable verbal handle.
The endpoint branch supplies the edge that discourse cannot independently fix.

changed_reading.before: Mursaha is only an asked-for event time, and dhikraha is only mention.
changed_reading.after: The focus may expose a demand that speech itself moor the event by fixing one edge: the addressee can mention it but cannot supply that stabilizing terminus.

strongest_changes: The focus becomes a role boundary: endpoint-fixing belongs with the Lord, while the addressee's relation is warning and reminding.
Dhikra becomes proleptic, preparing the future moment when each person remembers their own striving under unveiled consequence.
The Moses report-to-example arc makes mention a transformative warning form rather than date-information.
summary.what_was_special: The strongest activation came from separating two operations hidden in dhikra: making an event present in speech or memory versus fixing its endpoint. Repeated r-s-w also opened a contained material-to-discursive mooring echo.
remaining_uncertainties: The ellipsis in fima anta min permits both rebuke and role delimitation.
The packet's s-w-a inventory supplies no temporal-hour branch, so the feminine referent rests on local wording and pronoun continuity rather than that branch inventory.
The r-s-w report branch is exploratory and should not displace the surface mooring sense.
